verdict.rationale: BigQuery's own Iceberg managed tables keep data in the open Iceberg format in customer-owned storage buckets, readable by open-source and third-party engines. Query results can also be retrieved in Apache Arrow format. This gives a real open-format exit path, but only for data held in Iceberg tables, not for all standard tables. One user's remark that migrating off BigQuery 'would likely take months' is general lock-in sentiment, not a documented export failure. Missing for 10: documented bulk export of all standard tables to open formats (e.g., Parquet/Avro/CSV to object storage), coverage of all data types and metadata, an off-boarding workflow, and independent hands-on corroboration of a full exit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Iceberg managed tables offer the same fully managed experience as standard BigQuery tables, but store data in customer-owned storage buckets.
Iceberg managed tables support the open Iceberg table format for better interoperability with open-source and third-party compute engines on a single copy of data.
You can now retrieve query results directly in the Apache Arrow format for faster retrieval speed and improved serialization efficiency.
